message:
I see. In the original code, `a` had `num_coords` elements and `c` had `num_coords` elements. The loop `for (int i = num_segments - 1; i >= 0; i--)` accesses `c[i+1]` and `a[i+1]`. When `i = num_segments - 1 = num_coords - 2`, `c[i+1] = c[num_coords-1]` which is valid since `c` has `num_coords` elements.

Now let me look at the current (vulnerable) version. In the current code, `segments` is a single vector of `Segment` structs with `num_coords` elements. After `pop_back()`, it has `num_coords - 1 = num_segments` elements. Then the loop accesses `segments[i+1]` for `i = num_segments-1`, which is `segments[num_segments]` - out of bounds!

Wait, but let me check the intermediate commits. Let me look at the commit that introduced the `segments` struct:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/librawspeed && git show 3abae6ed -- src/librawspeed/common/Spline.h | head -200</｜｜DSML｜｜>
